text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic is the official candidate of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia for president of Yugoslavia. The main board of the ruling DPS of Montenegro, the other federal unit, will decide whether to support the move at a session to be held later.
- Greek telecommunications OTE and Italian Stet have clinched a deal to purchase 49 percent of Telecomm Srbije, the agreement is expected to be signed on Sunday.
- The SPS main board will discuss the privatisation law next week.
- Temporary licences will be issued to all radio and television stations, now operating illegally, that have met the necessary requirements, says Serbian Information Minister Radmila Milentijevic.
- Yugoslavia asked U.N. to extend its mandate in Eastern Slavonia.
- Over 1,000 workers of machine factory Lola blocked Belgrade-Obrenovac highway on Thursday, demanding six-months of unpaid wages and sacking of general manager Dragan Jovanovic.

- Serbian agriculture minister Jovan Babovic expects over 2.86 million tonnes of wheat to be harvested this year which will be enough to meet domestic needs and leave about one million tonnes for export.

- Bosnian Serb government passess regulation on establishment of trade relations with Yugoslavia without administrative restrictions in line with the special ties agreement between the two countries. The regulation comes into force on June 9.
- Yugoslavia will start issuing new passports on June 16, the federal government decided.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic will visit Poland from June 12-13 and is due to sign agreeements on double taxation avoidance, agriculture and tourism.
- U.N. Human Rights Rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn says it is unacceptable to speak about collective guilt for war crimes and urged for individuals to be brought to the Hague.
- Serbian government soon to draft programme for promotion of exports.
- Industrial production is in recession, Institute of Economic Sciences says in its monthly report.
- Yugoslav banking card YUBA expected to be issued this summer by commercial banks and the Postal Savings Bank.
BORBA
- The strength of the left is growing, says president of directorate of Yugoslav Left (Jul) Mira Markovic.
BLIC
- Colonel Veselin Sljivancanin, indicted for war crimes, says he is ready to go to the Hague if that is needed to spare the Serb people from bearing consequences.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Two day Serb-Kosovo Albanian talks in Athens, held under the auspices of German foundation Berthelsmann, ended without any results.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Serbian pension fund secures short-term credit of 479 million dinars to pay half of March pensions even though its account was already 3.4 billion dinars in the red.
- Two kilometer long and 15 meter wide oil slick on Sava river near Belgrade, polluter unknown.
- Asbestos and other toxic waste stored only several kilometers from centre of town of Mladenovac.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA
- SPS officially nominated Slobodan Milosevic as federal President during a visit of its delegation to Podgorica.
- Amendments to the federal constitution are undesirable for the DPS, said DPS vice-president Milica Pejanovic-Djurisic.
MONITOR

- After his visit to the Hague Montenegrin public prosecutor Vlado Susovic said he was opposed to a court decision to hand over Nebojisa Ranisavljevic, indicted for killing train passengers in Strpci, to a Serbian court.
- Police arrested a former minister Nebojisa Zekovic in a clampdown on crime. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
